articles.title_orig: Pope returns to Vatican days after surgery; surgeon says he should be fit for Latin America tour
articles.title_zh: Pope returns to Vatican days after surgery; surgeon says he should be fit for Latin America tour
articles.content_orig:
âI would say there are no clinical reasons why this visit should not take place.â
Professor Stefano Margaritora, the surgeon who operated on Pope Leo XIVâs lung on Tuesday, October 13, told Vatican News that, from a medical standpoint, the Pope can undertake the demanding visit to Latin America scheduled for November 6â17.
Dr. Margaritora is Professor of Thoracic Surgery at the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart and Director of the Thoracic Surgery Unit at the Agostino Gemelli University Hospital Foundation.
Q: Professor, first of all, how is Pope Leo XIV?
At the time of his discharge from the hospital, Pope Leo was in entirely satisfactory clinical condition. His blood test results were completely normal, and his heart function was fine.
The lungâs re-expansion after surgery is proceeding according to the usual timetable. So, overall, his condition is good.
Q: Can you tell us how the lung adenocarcinoma was discovered?
The discovery of the Popeâs malignant lung tumor was entirely accidental, as unfortunately often happens.
During routine abdominal examinations, this small spot was found in the chest, at the base of the lung. This is fairly normal because, when radiological examinations of the abdomen are performed, the lower part of the lungs is usually visible, since the diaphragm is shaped somewhat like a parachute.
However, if this small spot had been a little higher up, it certainly would not have been seen.
Q: What does the Holy Fatherâs experience over the past few weeks teach us? How important is prevention?
Prevention is extremely important. The Holy Father falls into the category of people who discover they have lung cancer entirely by chance â not because they are undergoing preventive screening, but because they undergo examinations for other reasons.
For example, someone falls from a tree, goes to the emergency room for an X-ray, and a spot on the lung becomes visible. Or it is found during tests carried out for other reasons.
It would therefore be important for people, especially those at risk, to undergo regular preventive checkups â not only for other cancers for which widespread screening exists, such as breast or colon cancer, but also for lung cancer.
Unfortunately, especially in its early stages, this cancer causes no symptoms. We saw that in the Holy Fatherâs case: he had no respiratory symptoms and felt perfectly well.
Q: How would you describe the surgery? Was it a complicated operation?
It would be dishonest of me to say it was very complicated in order to make it sound heroic. In fact, the Holy Fatherâs operation was routine in the sense that, in similar cases involving a lung tumor of a certain size, the entire lobe containing it has to be removed.
In the Holy Fatherâs case, that was the lower lobe of the right lung. So, from that standpoint, it was a routine operation.
Q: Are you satisfied with the outcome of the surgery, Professor?
Yes, very much so. The operation went ahead without any complications, and that is what we always hope for before every operation. Unfortunately, that is not always how things go.
Q: Are you pleased with his postoperative recovery?
Yes, we are truly pleased with it. The Holy Father has put his heart and soul into his recovery, as the most motivated people do after this kind of operation.
As a result, he needed very little assistance from us. His determination to recover quickly has been effective in every respect. It was truly commendable.
Q: Can you estimate how long his recovery will take? Will he be ready in time for the visit to Latin America?
Treating him as I would any other patient, I think it takes a couple of weeks to make a truly complete physical recovery after this kind of operation. Since almost a week has already passed, I believe the Pope could be fully recovered in another ten days or so.
As for a long trip involving air travel in about three weeks, I would say there are no clinical reasons why it should not take place.
Q: What did it mean to you, as a man, a doctor, and a believer, to lead the team that operated on the Pope?
Operating on a Pope stirred a deep feeling that I cannot even describe. Obviously, the person before you is a man â after all, the Pope is a man â but you know very well that he is not an ordinary person. Pope Leo has such charisma that it would be impossible to regard him as ordinary.
You are about to operate on a Pope who, for the first time â at least in modern history â is undergoing surgery for a malignant tumor. As far as we know, that has never happened before.
You know the eyes of the world are on you, because he is (not) only a head of state: he is the leader of faithful spread throughout the world, and there is enormous media attention. So, it is clear that an operation that is routine medically cannot feel routine on a human level.
Therefore, I experienced a series of conflicting thoughts, telling myself: âYou have to perform a normal operation, one you have done a thousand times in your life,â and, âFor the first time, you are performing this kind of operation on a Pope.â
Q: May I ask what you said to the Pope just before the anesthesia took effect?
When the Pope entered the operating room, he was very down-to-earth and smiling. We had formed a sort of semicircle â my colleagues and I, the anesthesiologists, and the operating room staff.
When he came in, he looked around and saw us, and I said to him, âHoly Father, this is our dream team.â He smiled, and he let himselfâ¦ We began administering the anesthesia.
Q: Professor, may I ask what kind of patient Pope Leo XIV was during his days at Gemelli?
Pope Leo was an ideal patient. I am not saying that to flatter him. He truly did not cause the slightest problem for the team caring for him, and he would not have done so even if his name had been Mario Bianchi.
He was always serene, always smiling, and rarely complained, despite the pain a person inevitably feels, even with all the measures we take.
He followed every stage of our guidance on diet and physiotherapy. He got back on his feet and always did a little more than we asked of him.
On the second day after the operation, we turned around and found him arranging the chairs in the chapel himself. We said, âHoly Father, we can do that.â And he replied, âIt doesnât matter. I can do it, so I will.â What can I say? He really was an absolutely ideal patient.
I would also like to thank all the staff, the entire team at Gemelli Hospital who helped care for the Holy Father. We should never forget that, in hospitals, behind the work of the surgeon and the anesthesiologist, there are operating room nurses and other operating room staff, laboratory technicians, and radiology technicians, who came every day to take the Holy Fatherâs X-ray. There are physiotherapists and many other healthcare professionals who may not usually be mentioned, but whom I am glad to recognize.
I also want to express my heartfelt thanks to the leadership of the Gemelli Hospital Foundation and to the Rector of the Catholic University. They placed their trust in me and allowed me to have this truly extraordinary experience.
Thank you for reading our article. You can keep up-to-date by subscribing to our daily newsletter. Just click here .

articles.title_orig: Apple Retail Staff Told to Warn Against iPhone Duo Walk-In Purchases
articles.title_zh: Apple Retail Staff Told to Warn Against iPhone Duo Walk-In Purchases
articles.content_orig:
Some Apple retail employees have been told to warn customers against visiting to purchase an iPhone Duo without a pre-order on Friday, October 23.
Apple Store employees told MacRumors that they have been advised that there will likely be no ‌iPhone Duo‌ stock available for walk-in purchases on launch day. Staff have been instructed to discourage customers without pre-orders from coming in expecting to buy the device, warning that they will be disappointed.
Apple's online store tells customers to check back on Saturday, October 24 for pickup availability. Pickup reservations were briefly available when pre-orders opened before the option was disabled.
The October 24 message does not guarantee stock will be available that day, and it remains unclear how firm the warning shared with employees is and whether it applies worldwide. If the guidance is firm and widely perpetuated, it closes off a potential route for customers hoping to bypass the device's lengthy online wait times, at least at the stores concerned.
Warnings about a constrained launch began well before Apple announced the ‌iPhone Duo‌. In early September, Nikkei Asia reported that production had reached only a few hundred devices per day in late August. Further production problems emerged in late September.
Earlier this month, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman said Apple had at one point believed production constraints could push the start of sales into November. The company subsequently assembled enough inventory to proceed with the October 23 launch, although supply remained very limited .
The extent of the shortage became apparent when pre-orders opened earlier this week. Delivery estimates moved beyond launch day within minutes, and within 30 minutes, all configurations in Apple's U.S. online store showed January 25 shipping estimates. The device is now effectively sold out for Christmas through Apple's online store.
Apple subsequently described demand as " nothing short of extraordinary " in a statement to the Financial Times , adding that it was working to get devices to customers as quickly as possible. Apple has not publicly specified whether any stores will have stock for launch-day walk-in purchases.
The ‌iPhone Duo‌ starts at $1,999 in the United States, with the first pre-order deliveries scheduled for October 23.

articles.title_orig: Trump promises big investment in KY facility 'if the Republicans win'
articles.title_zh: Trump promises big investment in KY facility 'if the Republicans win'
articles.content_orig:
Meanwhile, top Democrats are ramping up their travel schedule as the party grows more optimistic about flipping the House and Senate.
• Trump’s red-state rally: President Donald Trump held an event in Kentucky this afternoon, continuing a series of campaign stops in mostly conservative strongholds. The president promised his latest gift to voters if Republicans are victorious in the midterms: a $100 million investment in a pharmaceutical plant in the Bluegrass State.
• Jackson doubles down: Meanwhile, Maine Senate Democratic nominee Troy Jackson told CNN’s Dana Bash that he had no regrets telling his Republican opponent, Sen. Susan Collins, to “shut up” at their debate earlier this week.
• Heated town hall exchange: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist political movement, during a heated exchange at a town hall.
Michigan Senate Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed stopped short of criticizing the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee as he continues to be outspent by Republican opponent Mike Rogers.
“They’ve been really supportive; we’ve got to do all we can collectively to make sure we win this race,” El-Sayed told CNN at a campaign event in Caro, Michigan.
Rogers, the Republican nominee for US Senate in Michigan, announced plans this week for a seven-figure ad buy to promote his closing message in the final weeks of the battleground race.
Rogers’ expenditure for the closing stretch adds to an already massive GOP effort in Michigan. In the final three weeks, Republicans are set to spend more than $29 million total on ads, including outside groups, while Democrats have about $18 million booked, CNN previously reported.
“The reality of it is also they don’t really have a message, right? Their message is they don’t like me, but that doesn’t fix your gas or your groceries, so they can spend all the money they want on Mike Rogers’ message,” El-Sayed said Saturday.
On campaigning with Stevens: El-Sayed also told CNN today he would campaign with his former Democratic primary opponent Haley Stevens if the opportunity came up.
“I’m grateful for her support, and I really appreciate just how quickly she endorsed us,” El-Sayed said.
Stevens could offer help among voters El-Sayed has struggled to win over, including Jewish and Black voters, who largely backed Stevens, underscoring lingering tensions within Michigan Democrats’ traditional coalition that she may be positioned to bridge.
CNN’s David Wright contributed to this post.
With less than three weeks until the midterms, Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for Ohio governor, campaigned Saturday evening in a blood-red part of this state, showing how Republicans everywhere are trying to motivate their base in a tough political environment.
“The biggest concern Republicans have right now are getting people out to vote,” Jay Edwards, a fellow GOP statewide candidate, said as he introduced Ramaswamy for a town hall here in Monroe County, which gave President Donald Trump nearly 80% of the vote in 2024.
Ramaswamy repeatedly paid homage to rural Ohio and the Appalachian region. He promised he was “not running to be the mayor of greater Columbus” and that rural Ohio is the “backbone of our state.”
Ramaswamy, the former 2024 presidential candidate and short-lived leader of Trump’s Department of Government Efficiency, will need strong turnout to overcome Democratic nominee for governor Amy Acton in what polls show is a tight race . Ramaswamy and Acton, the former director of the Ohio Department of Health, are vying to succeed term-limited GOP Gov. Mike DeWine.
Ramaswamy promised at the town hall to be “the most conservative governor we have ever seen in the history of our state,” suggesting past Ohio GOP leaders have not been bold enough. And he said Acton would be “the first socialist governor” of Ohio — a label she rejects — while repeatedly knocking her for refusing to debate him.
“If you cannot do a debate, you cannot lead this state,” he said.
Acton has defended her decision not to debate Ramaswamy, calling him a “chronic liar.”
Maine Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson told CNN’s Dana Bash on Saturday he doesn’t regret telling his opponent, GOP Sen. Susan Collins, to “shut up” during a debate this week.
Collins accused Jackson of setting up a protester outburst in the crowd during the Thursday debate. The protester shouted at Collins about the impact of data centers.
Jackson told Bash that “I had no idea who it was,” continuing that he “was surprised whenever he jumped up.”
“I’ve had four debates with Sen. Collins. I’ve shook her hand afterwards every time. But what I’m not going to be is, you know, talked down to by Sen. Collins,” Jackson said, adding, “I’m not going to apologize for that, no.”
Bash followed up by asking Jackson whether this was another example of aggressive behavior that he has been accused of by some colleagues from his time in the state legislature. Jackson denied those allegations, saying, “Some Republicans have been spending millions of dollars attacking me and my family, making untrue claims.”
Bash’s full interview with Jackson will air on CNN’s “State of the Union” on Sunday at 9 a.m. ET.
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed was pressed by a town hall attendee Saturday over his disavowal of the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist political movement.
Seconds after El-Sayed finished stumping in Caro, Michigan, a man shouted from the crowd, “Abdul, will you disavow the Muslim Brotherhood?”
El-Sayed, who could make history as the first Muslim elected to the Senate, has frequently faced Republican accusations that he is sympathetic to interests connected to Islamic terror.
The question Saturday prompted a heated exchange as the attendee repeatedly pressed El-Sayed about the Muslim Brotherhood, saying he had yet to hear the candidate disavow the organization.
El-Sayed, after disavowing the movement, blasted the man for implicitly assuming his “dual loyalty.”
“You assume … that because I am Muslim, that somehow I would have some allegiance to something that is not our Constitution,” El-Sayed said. “For me, that Constitution is the guiding light.”
The audience member walked out after the exchange as the crowd cheered for El-Sayed.
The nominee has faced questions about potential connections to the organization. The latest attacks came after old tweets from El-Sayed’s half-sister resurfaced online, including a post from 2012 in which she described having “an amazing talk with my mom about her activism in the Muslim Brotherhood during the early 70s while she was in college.”
Earlier this week, El-Sayed denied allegations that he or his family has ties with the Muslim Brotherhood, telling reporters on Thursday that to think that anybody in his family was part of the organization was “an insane thing to assume.”
Republican Sen. Darline Graham of South Carolina, who was appointed to fill her late brother’s seat and is now running for a full term, broke with President Donald Trump over his executive order waiving sanctions on Russian fossil fuel sales. The sanctions bill was named after her brother.
“The president and I share the same goal, which is to end the war, get gas and diesel prices down. And the sanctions bill is one of the tools he can use to do that,” Graham told reporters at an event Saturday in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina.
“I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia to end the war and get the gas prices down because I don’t trust Putin and I don’t trust Russia,” she said, referring to President Vladimir Putin.
She said she looks forward to talking to Trump when he’s in South Carolina to campaign with her next week.
Some context: The waiver announced in an executive order Friday comes as Trump increasingly feuds with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky  and as cracks appear in Washington’s support for Kyiv in its yearslong war against its invading neighbor.

articles.title_orig: ICE Vehicle Sales Crash 49%(!) While EV Share Jumps to 67%(!) — China EV Sales Report for September
articles.title_zh: ICE Vehicle Sales Crash 49%(!) While EV Share Jumps to 67%(!) — China EV Sales Report for September
articles.content_orig:
High gas prices and a never-ending wave of new BEVs has allowed September to reach 67% EV market share, a new record!
However, while record market share was achieved in the past thanks to strong EV sales, this time, the record achievement is thanks to a significant ICE (internal combustion engine) crash. The overall market dropped 28% year over year (YoY), to around 1.6 million sales. Plugins were down 17% YoY, but pure ICE sales were much worse off, crashing 49% YoY!
Adding 45% BEV share to PHEVs (22% share) meant that, in September, a record 67% of all cars sold in China had a plug! If this trend continues in the future, the Chinese market will be fully electrified by 2030, and will be 100% BEV before 2035!
This great result pulled the 2026 share up, to 58%, already 4% above the full year result of 2025. BEVs on their own were up to 39% (versus 33% in 2025).
At this pace, I expect the final number for 2026 EV share in China to be above 60%, with BEVs alone north of the 40% mark. And when the largest global automotive market gets this electrified … then the ICE industry is in serious trouble.
The ICE extinction is also visible in the overall ranking. Although, this month, we should highlight that two ICE models reached the top 10, both coming from the Toyota stable — the Corolla Cross in 8th and the RAV4 in 10th.
Although it might seem strange to highlight the fact that ICE models reached the overall top 10, this follows the same logic of “news is not when a dog bites a man, but when a man bites a dog,” meaning that in the last few months it has become normal to have a 100% plugin overall top 10 in China, so when ICE models return to the top 10, it is news , because that is no longer the norm.
Looking at the best sellers in several size categories , the ICE extinction is also quite visible. Although, once again, the C-segment/compact category is the exception, with the only ICE representative showing up there — the Toyota Corolla Cross, in 2nd, behind the leader Nevo Q05 and just ahead of the BYD Dolphin.
Having a quick look at the five size categories, the highlight is the smaller category, which is finally back to decent volumes. The Bestune Xiaoma showed up in a surprising 2nd place.
Another highlight is the fact that the new BYD Great Tang, the automaker’s new flagship SUV, joined the podium — in 3rd, behind the Xiaomi BEV models.
Here’s more info and commentary on September’s top selling electric models:
The extended wheelbase version, imaginatively called “L,” is helping the Model Y’s fortunes in China. In September, deliveries reached 50,359 units , which allowed it to win the monthly best seller prize. Nonetheless, deliveries slid 2% compared to September 2025. The long-wheelbase version is proving to be of big help to the US crossover, keeping the Model Y’s sales afloat, but new variants can only do so much. When most direct competitors are transitioning to 800V platforms and adding new features, the six-year-old Model Y is starting to look a bit old. Still, the Tesla crossover has enough demand to provide it a podium position this year. Next year, though? Hard to see it getting there.
A BYD Dolphin for BYD Seagull money ($10,000) . This was Geely’s internal memo to describe the formula for the Geely Xingyuan when developing its star model. With an interesting name — Xingyuan translates as “wishing upon a star” — it seems that Geely had its wish granted. However, the Geely model lost the best seller trophy in September, with its 44,275 registrations representing an 8% drop YoY. Proof that the competition never sleeps in China, Geely’s hatchback now has to deal with Leapmotor’s B-segment contenders, the A10 and A05; the new-generation Wuling Bingo; Chery’s new QQ3; let’s not forget about BYD’s Yuan Up; and, above all, there’s the new-generation BYD Seagull, which has just one goal — to steal the Xingyuan’s best seller crown in 2026.
BYD’s midsize SUV continues to implement the transition to the new generation. Thanks to the ramp-up of the new Ultra body, BYD’s star player was 3rd, scoring 30,603 registrations . Sales were up by 25% compared to the same month last year. Once the new generation is fully ramped up, the Song will once again be a fierce adversary for the competition to beat. The new Ultra generation features lidar and 1,500 kW DC charging, and these two features aren’t even the most impressive aspect of the model! That would be the price. It starts at 152,000 yuan (or $22,000) with the 76 kWh battery, and it goes up to 180,000 yuan (or $26,000) with the 83 kWh battery. For comparison, the Tesla Model Y starts in China at 259,000 yuan ($38,250)…. Expect the Song to experience a second youth in the second half of the year, and while it is impossible to displace the Tesla Model Y from the runner-up spot, the last place on the podium is doable this year. And maybe gold in 2027?
BYD’s premium arm Fang Cheng Bao has a success on its hands. This big Land Rover SUV, the Ti (Tai?) 7, scored 27,544 registrations last month, a new year best. The BEV versions of this Chinese Defender were recently launched (92 & 106 kWh batteries), including with Flash Charging technology, and they have been selling like hot cakes now that the market is shifting to pure electrics. Thanks to a successful (and boxy) design, competitive specs, and a nice interior, for its price range, this is one of those models that just begs to be sent overseas — going after not only the posh SUVs of premium brands, but also the gas guzzling Land Cruisers and Patrols of this world.
BYD’s small crossover continues to surprise, thanks to recently improved specs. BYD’s team player rose to 5th in September, scoring 22,767 registrations , which nevertheless was a 12% decline YoY…. Despite not being the most exciting vehicle to look at, or drive, the truth is that it scores high in value for money, with prices starting at $11,000 and higher end versions having BYD’s driver-assistance system. With small vehicles currently having a moment in China, expect the small crossover to show up in the top 5 from time to time.
Looking at the rest of the best seller table, the highlight is without a doubt the brand new MG 07, which landed with a bang by delivering a significant 14,577 units right in its landing month.
With a sporty design that reminds one of a certain model from a certain Stuttgart brand, the truth is that the attractive midsize fastback has everything to challenge the category leaders — the Xiaomi SU7, BYD Seal 06, and Tesla Model 3. It is sold both in PHEV and BEV versions, especially considering that it has a waiting list in the tens of thousands.
As for the second half of the table, two small BEVs deserve a mention. The new Chery QQ3 EV was in 18th thanks to a record 12,688 registrations, while FAW’s Bestune Xiaoma had a surprise appearance on the table, in 20th, thanks to some 12,500 registrations.
Outside the top 20, the main event was the ramp-up of Xpeng’s new baby, the Mona L03, which with some 12,000 registrations in September sure looks close to joining the top 20. The same can be said about the Leapmotor A05, which had around the same number of deliveries as the Mona L03. It is another Leapmotor model close to joining the table soon.
This was a month with plenty of significant debuts. Besides the aforementioned MG 07, a few other models started their careers on a high note. There’s Xiaomi’s Sky Nomad twins (the N70 had some 7,000 deliveries, while the larger N90 had around 5,000). There’s also the Geely Galaxy TT, the make’s answer to the Xiaomi SU7, which had close to 7,000 deliveries — a similar number to the VW ID.ERA 5S, Volkswagen’s latest attempt to stop the sales bleeding and convince previous VW Lavida owners to stay with the brand.
Looking at the 2026 ranking , the podium remained the same, and unless something unexpected happens, it should stay as it is until the end of the year, with the small Geely repeating its 2025 win. That also means the Tesla Mode

With gas prices topping $6 a gallon and an unpopular war continuing in Iran, President Trump’s approval has slipped with California Republicans — a falloff that could diminish the party’s chances in the state’s few competitive congressional races.
A new poll by the UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies, co-sponsored by The Times,  found that 76% of Republican voters in the state approve of the president’s performance, down from 83% last year.
The president’s approval has softened even among those who still support his performance. Only 44% of Republicans in California said they strongly support Trump’s performance, down from 57% who said the same in August 2025.
That could translate into lower Republican turnout in the state’s few competitive races, said the poll’s director, Mark DiCamillo.
“Republicans are losing some of their enthusiasm in terms of being motivated to vote,” he said.
In addition, the more Trump tries to make the midterm elections about himself — such as the pro-Trump ads recently sponsored and paid for by the government — the more Democrats might be inclined to show up, said G. Cristina Mora, the UC Berkeley institute’s co-director.
“That might actually have a galvanizing effect on voters,” she said.
Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton are competing in the race for California governor. Here’s what you need to know about the candidates.
Trump’s sinking support in California mirrors a national decline in the president’s approval, even among Republicans.
The congressional map in the state was already challenging for Republicans after voters last year approved a referendum championed by Gov. Gavin Newsom to redraw districts to be more favorable for Democrats — a response to similar efforts by Republicans in Texas and other states.
In the new map, only four of the state’s 52 districts are currently considered safe Republican districts, while three additional districts are seen as competitive , according to the Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan political handicapper.
The remaining 45 districts are seen as either likely or solidly Democratic in a state where Democrats hold a roughly 20% advantage in party registration.
Only one race is considered by Cook to be a true toss-up — California’s 22nd Congressional District in the Central Valley, which is held by Republican Rep. David Valadao.
“We’re looking at the best case scenario for Democrats at this point,” said Erin Covey, Cook’s U.S. House editor.
Valadao, one of only 10 Republicans to vote for Trump’s impeachment in the wake of the Jan. 6, 2021, insurrection, faces progressive Democrat Randy Villegas, a political science professor who has the backing of  Bernie Sanders. The Vermont senator is joining Villegas this weekend for a rally in Bakersfield.
Valadao first won a seat in Congress in 2012, but was ousted from office during the Democrats’ “blue wave” election in 2018, in which the party gained 40 seats in the House in the first election after Trump took office in 2016. Valadao was able to win back his seat in 2020 and has held it  since.
As Californians prepare to elect a new governor in November, the top concern they want the new leader to prioritize is reducing the state’s entrenched high cost of living, according to a new poll.
There has been scant public polling in the race, but a poll conducted in June by a political committee backing Villegas showed the Democrat holding a  4-point lead over Valadao.
Two other congressional districts in the state are listed by Cook as leaning Democratic:
Trump’s approval also dipped among Black and Latino voters in the poll.  Both groups were part of Trump’s winning coalition in the 2024 presidential election.
The poll also found broad disapproval of two signature Trump administration policies.
It found that 70% of California voters disapprove of Trump’s decision to go to war in Iran, including 1 in 5 Republicans.
Also, 70% of California voters believe that the president’s immigration policies are hurting California’s economy and local businesses, including 1 in 5 Republicans.
The poll was conducted online in English and Spanish between Sept. 15 and Sept. 20 and included the opinions of 6,989 registered California voters. The margin of error is plus or minus 1.5 percentage points.

articles.title_orig: In Kentucky midterm campaign stop, Trump says he "can do stuff that is unbelievable"
articles.title_zh: In Kentucky midterm campaign stop, Trump says he "can do stuff that is unbelievable"
articles.content_orig:
President Trump touted his power in his second go-around in the White House Saturday while rallying in Kentucky to bolster Republican turnout as his party struggles in the midterms, saying, "I can do stuff that is unbelievable."
Mr. Trump, who spoke in the city of Highland Heights to boost Republican candidates, including Ed Gallrein for the U.S. House, was riffing on his decision to change how the U.S. government refers to the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America .
"I don't think I could have done this in my first term. This is a much more powerful term," Mr. Trump said. "Google wouldn't have taken my call in the first. Now, they kiss my ass."
"Well, I also changed the name of a lake in Canada to the Lake America," he continued, referring to Lake Ontario .
Mr. Trump's self-proclaimed power is set against voter frustration with how he's wielded it, with tariffs and the Iran war driving up prices and more Americans seeing the president looking out for his own interests and not those of the country.
With control of both chambers of Congress on the line , and with it the prospects of Democratic-led investigations of his administration should they win, Mr. Trump has put himself at the fore for voters even as Republicans privately worry he's a liability.
Mr. Trump nominated one of his personal lawyers to serve as attorney general, ordered military strikes on accused drug-smuggling boats, is trying to put his name on the Kennedy Center , and has enriched himself and his family while he's been in office.
While meandering through topics onstage in Kentucky, Mr. Trump touched on gas prices, saying that the war with Iran was going to end soon — an assertion he's made many times over the course of the nearly eight-month conflict — and that gas prices will drop to lower than previously. The crowd cheered.
Mr. Trump rehashed his dubious promise that if Republicans win the House and the Senate, then every adult American would get $5,000. That would most likely cost more than $1 trillion and require congressional approval, while exacerbating the country's nearly $1.8 trillion annual budget deficit.
At Saturday's rally, Mr. Trump added a new conditional promise for Kentucky; if Republicans win, he said, the Department of Defense would invest in revitalizing a drug manufacturing facility in the state.

articles.content_orig:
Musk says Roadster owners can command the unveiling stunts autonomously, with a Texas looping track.
Elon Musk says owners of the new Tesla Roadster will be able to ask the car to perform the stunts Tesla showed at its unveiling, with the car doing the driving itself. Musk made the comment Saturday in a reply on X to tech blogger Robert Scoble, and he added a promise of a looping track at Tesla’s Texas headquarters.
Scoble had argued that the person in the Roadster is not really driving it. In his description, the driver operates a computer that tells another computer what to do, with steering, braking and acceleration all handled by wire. Musk answered, “True. You will be able to ask the Roadster to perform any of the tricks shown autonomously, as it will be sentient. Also, we will have a wild looping track (crazier even than Hot Wheels) at our Texas HQ where you can test out your Roadster.”
You will be able to ask the Roadster to perform any of the tricks shown autonomously, as it will be sentient.
Also, we will have a wild looping track (crazier even than Hot Wheels) at our Texas HQ where you can test out your Roadster.
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 17, 2026
At the October 15 event outside Waco, the car drove up a curved ramp until it was upside down, flew off on cold gas thrusters, flipped and landed. It also hovered over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Semi, Model Y and Model 3 while moving. As we noted in our breakdown of the three Roadster configurations , Musk said at the event that the car “literally is just going to puff itself up” to perform the maneuvers whenever an owner wants. Saturday’s reply adds that the car would run them on its own.
Tesla has described some of the hardware that would make that possible. The Roadster uses steer by wire with a yoke, and its cold gas thrusters rely on electric actuators for small adjustments in flight. A fan system under the car creates suction, which Tesla says is strong enough to hold it upside down, a setup we covered in our look at the Roadster’s fan system and thrusters .
Musk did not say when an autonomous stunt feature might arrive, how it would work, or what he means by sentient. He also gave no size, location or opening date for the Texas track. Production is planned for Giga Texas in 2027 or 2028, and Tesla says the car is not approved for public road use. The Rocket version, the one built to fly, is invite only.
The comment follows a week of Musk teasing the event, including his claim that the demo would be a banger, which we covered before the stream . Tesla reports third quarter earnings on October 21, and shareholders can submit and vote on questions through the Say portal until 4 p.m. EDT on October 20, according to our earnings Q&A preview . A question about autonomous Roadster stunts and the Texas track would be a quick way to get specifics from management.
Gene has been obsessed with cars since before he could legally sit in the front seat. Writer, researcher, unofficial CS support, accountant, native suit guy when needed, and overall stick poker. He approaches every story the way he approaches a road trip: with too much enthusiasm, not enough planning, and a surprisingly good outcome. gene@teslarati.com
Musk told users to ask Grok Bot to scrub their phone numbers from spam lists.
Elon Musk has a new use case for Grok Bot, and it is the spam call. On Thursday he replied to an X user named Arash with a short instruction: “Ask your @Grok @Bot to remove your phone number from spam call & text lists!” Arash had said he got tired of the calls, had an AI bot find his number on listing sites and file removal requests, and packaged the process as a free skill for others.
The skill is called Spam-Call Scrubber , which is described to find a phone number on people search sites and data brokers, submits the opt outs, completes the confirmation emails those sites send back, and rechecks on a schedule the user picks. Using it requires the Grok Bot app . The pitch is time saved, since most broker opt outs sit behind separate forms on separate sites.
Ask your @Grok @Bot to remove your phone number from spam call & text lists!
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 15, 2026
Musk said Grok Bot now gives each bot its own email address, and that it can detect scam emails. On Thursday he also said SpaceX would make users whole if the bot botches a purchase or leaks a card, then told users to shop away from Amazon after the retailer blocked the agent, as Teslarati reported . The terms of service we reviewed at the time put responsibility for what an agent does on the user.
For Tesla owners, Grok Bot is not just a phone app. Tesla brought Grok Bot into its vehicles on September 22 , and we argued earlier this week that the Cybercab’s real advantage may be the errands it runs during a ride . Every Cybercab and the rest of the Model Y Robotaxi fleet has it enabled. The more routine tasks like this one become, the more a rider has reason to hand over something personal in the back seat.
The new Spam-Call Scrubber skill can be downloaded for free and works on sites that honor removal requests, while noting that listings can reappear, and illegal robocallers do not check any registry. Whether Spam-Call Scrubber cuts anyone’s call volume is something the first wave of users will find out, and Musk’s endorsement guarantees that wave is coming.
Musk promises SpaceX will cover Grok Bot purchase errors, tells users to shop beyond Amazon.
Elon Musk said SpaceX will reimburse users if Grok Bot botches a purchase or leaks their card details. A few hours later he was telling users to take their shopping elsewhere after Amazon shut the agent out.
The first post was a reply to an X user who said Grok Bot booked him a flight after he sent a photo of his credit card. “This works well,” Musk wrote. “If Grok @Bot makes a mistake with a purchase or leaks your card (never happened yet), SpaceX will make you whole,” said Musk .
The second came after another user posted the error his Grok Bot hit on Amazon: “Continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed.” The user said his bots can no longer order from the site. Musk answered, “Just ask Grok @Bot to buy what you want someplace else and get a better deal. There are far more purchasing websites than just Amazon!” He later added, “Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon,” a possible hint at an X shopping service.
Just ask Grok @Bot to buy what you want someplace else and get a better deal.
There are far more purchasing websites than just Amazon!
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 15, 2026
The Amazon block did not start Thursday. A reply to Musk on October 10 said Amazon was blocking the bot, and Musk responded that Grok would find another way, then showed an order it placed on Lego’s website.
The latest reimbursement promise builds on late August when Musk told a Tesla investor weighing whether to give Grok Bot access to his bank accounts, “If Grok Bot messes up, we will make you whole,” as Teslarati covered when SpaceXAI added its Finance integration. That promise goes further than the company’s consumer terms, which make users responsible for what their agents do and generally cap liability at the greater of fees paid or $100. Neither Thursday post says those terms have changed, so for now it remains a statement on X rather than a published policy.
The two posts matter to Tesla owners because Grok Bot is no longer limited to a phone. Tesla brought it into its vehicles on September 22, and it is now enabled across every Cybercab and the rest of the Model Y Robotaxi fleet, as noted when Teslarati looked at why Grok Bot may be the Cybercab’s real advantage . A rider who asks for groceries or a coffee order is relying on retailers that let the agent in. Amazon has now said it will not, and Musk’s answer is to route around it.

Following a report that Samsung might skip the latest Snapdragon flagship, Qualcomm says that rumors about the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 running into overheating issues are “inaccurate.”
For context: Reports out of Korea suggest that Samsung is in talks with Qualcomm to address overheating issues with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 , with Samsung weighing its options and considering skipping the chip for its own Exynos 2700.
It’s a big claim, and one that Qualcomm says is “inaccurate.”
Responding to the story, Qualcomm tells 9to5Google that it is “proud of the innovation and strong momentum behind our next-generation flagship platform” and that reports of “thermal issues” are “inaccurate.”
Recent reporting about thermal issues related to Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is inaccurate. We are proud of the innovation and strong momentum behind our next-generation flagship platform and continue to work closely with global OEMs to deliver premium user experiences.
In a reply on Twitter/X, Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire reiterates that there are “no systemic thermal issues.”
There are no systemic thermal issues with the 8 elite gen 6. OEMs are consistently tuning their platforms as they launch their products. Always trying to balance performance and power to optimize their value props around different use cases. We work together to deliver the best…
Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 packs two 5GHz cores and some massive CPU and GPU performance improvements over the already-powerful Gen 5 flagship.
Devices already confirmed to use the new top-tier chip include Motorola Signature 27 , Xiaomi 18 , Redmagic 12 Pro Plus, Honor Magic 9 Pro Max , OnePlus 16 , and more.

articles.title_orig: Clashes, fires and looting break out as protesters rally across France, joining students
articles.title_zh: Clashes, fires and looting break out as protesters rally across France, joining students
articles.content_orig:
Riots broke out across major French cities on Saturday night as unrest spread beyond the capital, with government buildings torched and more than 1,000 people detained by police.
In the central city of Limoges, the historic town hall was set ablaze, with video showing its roof collapsing. In Marseille, black-clad protesters broke into city hall and defaced the building, and in Lyon, protesters torched the city’s tourist office, the Reuters news agency reported.
As night fell in Paris, groups of young people looted and started fires as protests ended, prompting police to respond with tear gas and baton charges in the narrow streets.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said 1,200 people had been detained nationwide in the unrest, and condemned the “unacceptable levels of violence.”
The destruction followed what had been largely peaceful protests, which have grown out of sweeping student-led rallies that gripped parts of France last month, sparking a broader movement against crumbling schools, the spiking cost of living, and perceived government inaction. The rallies have become emblematic of long-simmering, intergenerational anger among people who say their calls for social and political change are going unmet by negligent governments.
Some 550,000 protesters hit the streets across France, including 110,000 in Paris, interior minister Laurent Nunez said. Organizers estimated an even higher turnout.
“There’s an accumulation of wealth and power that’s completely out of control,” one protester, who gave her name as Pauline, told CNN in Paris on Saturday.
“We’re also here to support the youth. There are victories, but if we look at the bigger picture, it’s not going in the right direction,” the 36-year-old added.
Another demonstrator complained of “less democracy” and a “concentration of power” under President Emmanuel Macron’s leadership. “There are billionaires who control the media,” Louise, 38, told CNN. “We are fighting to change things.”
Macron slammed “sowers of chaos” for interfering with peaceful protests, and warned late on Saturday that “those who have broken, attacked (police) prefectures, as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished.”
“We do not back down in the face of rioters and those who’ve come to attack law enforcement,” said the Paris Police Prefecture – the body that oversees the Paris Police Force, emergency services and various other administrative departments – adding that its staffers stood “their ground with courage and professionalism.”
The police response to the weeks of protest has come under scrutiny. Earlier in the week, that response had left a 14-year-old boy with a fractured jaw. Another police officer was captured on camera using a headlock on a girl in the northwestern area of Alençon, an action now prohibited by law.
A protester in the city of Saint-Étienne, about 40 miles southwest of Lyon, lost his hand during a march there on Saturday, a police source told CNN affiliate BFMTV. This is the second reported instance of a demonstrator losing their hand in the current wave of student protests.
A student in the northeastern city of Lens lost his hand after reportedly picking up a grenade earlier this month, prompting the temporary suspension of one type of stun grenade by police. That ban, which still allowed police to use several different grenades, has now been rescinded.
Overall, authorities said that the “vast majority of individuals” had demonstrated peacefully on Saturday, according to BFMTV.
Posting on X, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the far-left La France Insoumise Party, emphasized that the majority of demonstrators on Sunday had made their point peacefully. “While news channels are flooded with images of violence in dozens of cities, everything is unfolding peacefully with tens of thousands of people calmly mobilized. Two worlds, two realities.”
Youth activists led solidarity protests in Belgium, Albania and Italy on Saturday as well.
Earlier this fall, high school students in France organized scattered protests demanding reduced class sizes, increased spending on teachers, investments in infrastructure designed to withstand the climate crisis and end to police violence against young people.
In the past decade and a half, a rise in fertility coupled with funding cuts has led to more students, but fewer teachers in classrooms. The French Education Minister Edouard Geffray has met with student protesters multiple times in recent weeks, although an agreement is yet to be made.

articles.title_orig: China's Star50 plunges as AI trade unravels
articles.title_zh: China's Star50 plunges as AI trade unravels
articles.content_orig:
China's AI play went from sprint to stumble. The Star50 soared roughly 75% from April to June, only to give back gains and slide close to 40% over the current half year. At its June 30 peak, the index traded at more than 80 times next 12 months' earnings, which left little margin once sentiment turned.
As investors reexamined demand and profit trajectories, China 's AI hardware names were hit hardest. MetaX Integrated Circuits Shanghai Co. and Moore Threads Technology Co. each dropped by about half in this stretch. The damage widened beyond one gauge too, with the hardware-tilted ChiNext off 36%. Fresh listings struggled: memory maker CXMT Corp., public since July, is 27% below its post-listing high, while robotics firm Yushu Technology Co. is roughly 50% under an August peak shortly after its IPO.
The pullback did not happen in a vacuum. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Jason Liao and Marvin Chen said a global selloff in AI hardware across the Nasdaq and Korea weighed most on China's onshore shares after foreign buyers crowded in during the second quarter.
The slide clashes with Beijing's plan to harness equities to accelerate tech leadership. Onshore IPOs have raised a combined $37 billion this year, the most in three years, with tech issuers bringing in over one third of that total. Fundraising matters because many of China's AI-linked national champions and startups favor selling stock over issuing debt, given higher global borrowing costs.
Flows flipped as prices fell. "It would be much harder for China to achieve its AI ambitions if technology stocks remain under pressure for an extended period," said Leonid Mironov of Gavekal Capital. "If the weakness goes on for more than six months, this will make fundraising difficult and also imply that the market is unimpressed with the technological progress being achieved."
When hype cycles meet reality, staying oriented takes help, so try the free Market Briefs newsletter for five-minute clarity each day
Officials are weighing stronger support. At a Thursday meeting on stabilization measures, financial regulators called on the national team to buy shares more aggressively. Mironov added that if the downturn drags on, Beijing may need to move faster on financial sector reforms and consider deploying the national team more forcefully.
Even after the drop, valuations remain rich. The Star50 trades above 40 times forward earnings. For context, South Korea's Kospi is under five times, while the Nasdaq 100 is at 21 times. Fund manager Jian Shi Cortesi called today's levels "a technical pullback, not a value play," and said, "For many high-potential tech names, big bargains won't appear until they fall another 30%-50%."
Earnings could shift the tone. Upside surprises in the upcoming third quarter reporting season might lift sentiment, while disappointments would tighten the funding vise. Watch foreign flows too. After a rush of second quarter buying, the sharp third quarter reversal left A-shares most exposed, matching the outflow data.
China wanted buoyant equity markets to bankroll AI expansion, and many companies leaned on issuing stock to do it. The rally stretched valuations, then momentum snapped. Now the trio to watch is clear: sentiment, earnings, and policy support. With the Star50 still priced for perfection and peers like the Kospi far cheaper, the risk profile across markets is not the same.

articles.title_orig: IMF-World Bank Meetings Focus on Global Risks and Potential Benefits of AI
articles.title_zh: IMF-World Bank Meetings Focus on Global Risks and Potential Benefits of AI
articles.content_orig:
BANGKOK, Oct. 17, 2026 (AP) — Guardrails are urgently needed to contain potential risks from the boom in artificial intelligence, the head of the International Monetary Fund said Friday, likening the technology to a Formula 1 race car that might go off the track and run people over.
“We are racing, and the question is how do we put barriers? So if a car was to fly out it doesn’t kill people,” IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said.
Sign up for Broadband and AI in the Next Congress on Dec 1!
“I have high respect for the industry. I think what you’re doing is incredibly important for humanity. You may give us the biggest gift, but if the car runs over people, that gift may not be so worthwhile,” she said while speaking on a panel on the impact of AI on the world economy along with experts including Anthropic co-founder and head of policy Jack Clark .
Clark is among technology industry leaders pushing for faster action on regulating AI. In a blog post last month, the rival to OpenAI proposed that the world’s top artificial intelligence companies come up with a coordinated way to pause development of advanced AI systems, warning the technology is improving so quickly there’s a risk humans would lose control .
“I think it’s worse than you describe. I think it’s Formula 1 at night without maybe brakes in the cars,” Clark said. “And it’s remarkable to me that the toys I buy for my children are regulated more than the literal superintelligence I work on at my day job.”
He added that the effort to build policy frameworks to regulate AI is underway.
“The world is now taking this seriously, and I think if we take it seriously, we are going to be able to get our arms around it,” Clark said. “But it cannot only be companies making these decisions. And if we’re negligent about this, we’re going to get some form of chaos.”
The impact of AI on jobs is yet to be fully understood, but an IMF study found three main trends. About 10% of jobs might be transformed or newly created, while work involving repetitive tasks will be gone, Georgieva said.
The third category will be service sector jobs generated by people who benefit from the investment boom.
“The net impact is positive," she said, though she added that “services don’t pay a lot.”
“So you get young people who normally would have gone into professional routine jobs now serving coffee in Starbucks. And that is not what I think young people in the world aspire for,” she said.
Tiff Macklem , the governor of the Bank of Canada, compared that to the effects on employment from more open trade, which has generated great global wealth and raised millions out of poverty. But many millions also lost their livelihoods as manufacturers moved jobs to China and other developing countries.
He said “in aggregate there is an overall benefit,” but acknowledged that in both trade and technology “there will be winners and losers.”
“You have to find a way to help the losers," Macklem said. “Without a system to help them cope with the loss you get a backlash.”
Dozens of people marched in Bangkok on Thursday and Friday in peaceful protests, seeking to draw attention to growing inequality and other frustrations.
Georgieva noted that to ensure that the benefits of AI can reach the maximum number of people, they have to have electricity and access to digital networks. Cybersecurity also is essential.
During the wide ranging session, the speakers were also asked about how they used AI in their own lives. Georgieva said she'd used it to track calories and lose weight.
The IMF chief, who has described her personal AI assistant as bossy, joked that she'd like AI agents to be more polite.
“I mean, the agents we get, they can be really annoying,” she said. “So can we work on, like, their manners?”
“We have this dial between sycophantic and rude,” he said. “So we'll spin it around the other way.”
This article was written by Elaine Kurtenbach of the Associated Press. AP journalists Haruka Nuga, Tian MacLeod Ji and Sakchai Lalit contributed.

articles.content_orig:

Republican U.S. Senate nominee Ken Paxton is setting off on an 18-day bus tour Saturday that will take him to over 30 stops across the state leading up to Election Day, according to plans first shared with The Texas Tribune Wednesday.
Paxton will kick off the “Come and Take It” bus tour in Rockwall two days before the start of early voting on Monday.
Evoking the Texas Revolution, Paxton’s closing message to Texans draws on his record as attorney general of suing opioid companies, Big Tech and the Biden administration: “When they come after Texans,” his campaign said, “Ken Paxton goes after them.”
He plans to close out the tour with a stop at the Alamo on Nov. 2, the eve of Election Day.
“In Texas, ‘come and take it’ has never been a slogan,” Paxton said in a statement. “It’s a promise.”
On Friday, Paxton’s opponent, Democrat James Talarico , announced his own get-out-the-vote push, dubbed the “Clear Eyes, Full Hearts” tour — a reference to Texas’ beloved Friday night lights football tradition.
“Texans are tired of being divided into teams — red versus blue, left versus right, rural versus urban,” Talarico said. “That’s why we’re traveling across the state to unite working people onto one team. I encourage Texans across the political spectrum to join us at one of our stops as we work to defeat the politics of division.”
Talarico plans to kick off his swing in Plano on Sunday and hit 20 cities before closing out in Austin the night before Election Day.
Paxton’s callback to symbols of Texan defiance are laden with symbolism as he finds himself in a dead heat with Talarico, who is seeking his party’s first statewide win since 1994. Public polls have shown the Austin lawmaker narrowly leading throughout the race, and Paxton has often framed the campaign as a last stand against a Democratic siege.
In a statement announcing his bus tour, Paxton contrasted his candidacy with that of Talarico, whom he accused of being “bankrolled by national Democrats and Silicon Valley billionaires” — a reference to LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman’s $11.5 million in donations to a super PAC supporting Talarico. (Talarico’s campaign has emphasized that the Austin Democrat “has no control over contributions to any super PAC” under federal law and wants to ban all super PACs.)
“He won’t fight for you. He’ll fight for them,” Paxton said. “So my message to anyone who comes after Texas is the same one Texans have been sending for almost two hundred years: Come and take it.”
National Republican power brokers, including President Donald Trump, Senate Republican leadership and Elon Musk, have poured over $214 million into Texas in recent weeks, tapping affiliated PACs to fund an advertising barrage aimed at promoting Paxton and attacking Talarico, according to media tracking firm AdImpact. Much of that spending has been backed by Musk , the Texas-based Tesla and SpaceX founder and the world’s richest man. In a Sept. 24 audio recording leaked to Politico last week, Paxton complained that his campaign was “all coming from D.C.”
Trump has made several stops in Texas now in a bid to gin up Republican turnout and support Paxton, following a midterm convention in Dallas that prominently featured the attorney general.
A prolific fundraiser, Talarico, meanwhile, is relying on his own campaign account for most of his ad spending, with $81 million booked on the airwaves so far. The super PAC in his corner has dropped an additional $8 million, while Senate Democratic leadership has put $3.5 million into the race so far.
Stops on Paxton’s tour will feature to-be-announced special guests and include events in the following cities: Dallas, Fort Worth, Houston, San Antonio, Austin, El Paso, Amarillo, Lubbock, Odessa, San Angelo, Abilene, Wichita Falls, Brownsville, McAllen, Laredo, Corpus Christi, Victoria, Tyler and Beaumont.

articles.title_orig: Leaked Gameplay Purports To Show A Canceled Assassin's Creed Game Set In Ancient China
articles.title_zh: Leaked Gameplay Purports To Show A Canceled Assassin's Creed Game Set In Ancient China
articles.content_orig:
At least there’s still Assassin’s Creed Jade to look forward to.
A mainline entry in the Assassin's Creed franchise set in ancient China might sound too good to be true. According to the some leaked footage of a reportedly canceled title called Assassin's Creed Destiny , that still may be the case. MP1st published a video showing off gameplay and placeholder footage of the allegedly scrapped Assassin's Creed game, which was reportedly being developed by Ubisoft and Tencent.
The video showed off the game's title, but also the 206 BCE setting during the Qin Empire in Ancient China. The gameplay footage shows the playable character scaling castle walls and performing stealth kills in typical Assassin's Creed fashion, while the placeholder videos offer a look at different combat skills and weapons, including a unique option that can only be described as a deadly umbrella.
With this Assassin's Creed game reportedly canceled, we may never see any of this footage make it out of the development graveyard. However, Ubisoft is still working on Assassin's Creed Jade , which was announced in 2022 as a mobile entry in the franchise that's set in ancient China. It's been several years since Ubisoft has revealed anything further about the project, but a 2024 Reuters report said it would be delayed until 2025. The developer still hasn't made any announcements about Assassin's Creed Jade , but a company exec recently told VGC that it would have co-op gameplay. If we're lucky, we might see some of the elements of the reported Assassin's Creed Destiny end up in the upcoming mobile game.

articles.title_orig: Fast-moving California wildfire burns homes as people are ordered to leave
articles.title_zh: Fast-moving California wildfire burns homes as people are ordered to leave
articles.content_orig:
Evacuation orders in California are in effect due to a rapidly growing wildfire that has already burned six homes south of Los Angeles.
The Norte Fire erupted on Friday in Orange County and quickly grew to 465 acres by the evening. By Saturday morning, it spread to 570 acres (2.3 sq km), with 5% containment.
One firefighter suffered heat exhaustion while battling the blaze.
Officials say the fierce Santa Ana winds will blow until Saturday, bringing further risk of more conflagrations.
The US National Weather Service (NWS) has issued a red flag warning for several California counties due to strong, gusty winds combined with low humidity and dry vegetation that create critical wildfire spread conditions.
The Norte Fire is one of 10 burning across the state, according to the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection.
In an update on Friday evening, Division 3 Fire Chief Mark Backoff said that six homes had either been damaged or destroyed by the Norte Fire, and one firefighter had been injured from heat exhaustion.
"We continue to engage in the firefight, and have additional resources coming," he said.
Footage posted online showed blazes tearing through homes in the communities of San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano.
The Bryson Fire, burning in the affluent coastal city of Malibu in Los Angeles county, has also sparked evacuation orders throughout the Santa Monica mountains and has grown to 147 acres, with 52% of the blaze contained.
More than 400 firefighters have been fighting the blaze.
Further south, the Henderson Fire in San Diego county erupted on Thursday, and has grown to over 3,100 acres (12.5 sq km), including around Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, with about 35% contained as of Saturday morning.
The size of the blaze has twice forced officials to close the I-5 highway, an important route that runs the length of the US West Coast.
The fires are being fanned by the Santa Ana winds, which normally begin during cooler months from late September to May.
Officials say the winds peaked on Friday, but will remain dangerous into early Saturday morning.
Winds topped 40mph (64km/h) in the Los Angeles area, the NWS said, adding that motorists should watch for debris blown into roadways.
Temperatures were far above average for this time of year in southern California, further driving up the fire danger.
The NWS has issued a heat advisory, saying that the danger of heat-related illness remained high.
Forecasts expect temperatures to reach 95F (35C) in southern California on Saturday.

articles.title_orig: Attorneys for Rep. Ilhan Omar accuse DOJ of violating judge's orders to follow protocols to protect her rights as member of Congress
articles.title_zh: Attorneys for Rep. Ilhan Omar accuse DOJ of violating judge's orders to follow protocols to protect her rights as member of Congress
articles.content_orig:
Attorneys for Representative Ilhan Omar have accused the Justice Department of violating a magistrate judge's order by failing to follow certain protocols designed to safeguard her constitutional interests as a member of Congress during the search of her home in Washington, D.C.
In the Oct. 16 letter, Omar's attorneys Amy Jeffress and Joshua Matz asked the government to immediately return the congresswoman's property, and they also demanded all video and audio recordings of the search be preserved.
"This vindictive, retributive, and politically motivated criminal investigation into one of the President's chief congressional critics violates Representative Omar's constitutional rights and threatens the separation of powers," they wrote in the letter, which was reviewed by CBS News.
In a statement, a Justice Department spokesperson disputed the claims in the letter, saying it was "riddled with false allegations and inaccuracies."
"Our attorneys and law enforcement partners complied with all court orders and legal obligations, as they always do," the spokesperson said. "Leaking a letter to the press right after sending it is not good faith. It is a publicity play."
Agents from the Homeland Security Investigations executed a search warrant at Omar's home on Monday, as part of a sprawling criminal investigation into her family's history for evidence of possible fraud and false statements in their immigration paperwork.
Her personal cellphone was among the materials seized in the search, CBS News previously reported , and grand jury subpoenas were also issued just days before the search to some of Omar's family members.
The search warrant was first presented to a magistrate judge in U.S. District Court about a week before it was executed.
Prosecutors and the judge engaged in a lengthy back-and-forth, after the judge raised concerns that the search warrant failed to incorporate any protocols to protect Omar's legislative privileges under the Constitution's speech and debate clause, CBS News previously reported.
Those protections stem from the 2007 United States v. Rayburn House Office Building D.C. Circuit Court case, which held that in a criminal investigation of a sitting member of Congress, the executive branch can't review information that is seized in a search without allowing that member to first screen it for legislative privilege.
Initially, prosecutors tried to argue the case shouldn't apply because the search was being carried out at Omar's home, and not at her congressional office, CBS News previously reported.
In the letter to the Justice Department, Omar's lawyers alleged several key requirements imposed by the judge had been violated.
HSI agents, for example, were supposed to notify both Omar and the House of Representatives Office of General Counsel of the execution of the search warrant — a step Omar's lawyers say never took place.
Agents also allegedly prevented her from contacting her attorney for more than an hour after the search started, the letter alleges, even though she and her counsel were supposed to be presented with a copy of the search warrant at the outset.
The timing of the search warrant and issuance of grand jury subpoenas in the case have raised eyebrows among many veteran former prosecutors.
Such overt investigative steps involving a sitting member of Congress so close to an election appear to run afoul of internal Justice Department guidelines, which state that prosecutors and agents should avoid taking overt investigative steps that could affect the outcome of an election or give one candidate an advantage or disadvantage.
Omar's lawyers also raised these same concerns in their letter to the department, saying: "Historically, the Department has refrained from this type of investigative activity so close to an election, so as to avoid even the appearance of politically motivated law enforcement actions. But the political motivations behind this pre-election investigation and search are clear as day. For the reasons given above, this search was neither justified nor lawful."
Omar has long been a frequent political target by President Trump and his allies. Mr. Trump has also made derogatory comments about her Somali heritage and her religion, and he has repeatedly accused her of immigration fraud.
"There is no legitimate basis for any suggestion that she has violated any law concerning her citizenship status," her attorneys wrote in the letter to DOJ, adding the search of her home "arose from a years-old, tired conspiracy theory concerning conduct stretching back decades."
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin made unusually public remarks about the nonpublic criminal investigation in a podcast on Friday, calling it a "strong case."
In an interview with Andrew Kolvet, who hosts "The Charlie Kirk Show," Mullin volunteered that multiple warrants had been served on Monday, adding that a judge had authorized the enforcement action and investigators expected to present their case to a grand jury.
It is unusual for federal officials to speak openly about ongoing criminal investigations beyond confirming a court-authorized search was conducted, in part due to due process protections and grand jury secrecy rules.

articles.title_orig: Zelensky says Musk-owned satellite system still restricted in Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Zelensky says Musk-owned satellite system still restricted in Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Ukraine is still unable to use its interceptor systems against Russian drones, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday, because of speed restrictions imposed on Starshield, an upgraded military version of Elon Musk's Starlink, amid an ongoing row with President Trump.
"Unfortunately, we can't use Starlink or Starshield technology on our territory today to shoot down jet-powered Shaheds," Zelenskyy said in an online group chat with reporters at the EU Summit. "They fly, and we can stop them with aircraft and other air defense, but we don't use Starlink for that, unfortunately. God willing, this will be restored."
Zelenskyy said Kyiv was discussing the issue with U.S. officials, and he was told the restrictions were linked to technical issues. The Ukrainian president added, however, that Starlink appears to be operating at higher speeds on European Union territory.
"Yes, we are in dialogue at the level of the military, the Ministry of Defense and diplomats, in touch with everyone including SpaceX. Nobody there is answering our military or the Ministry of Defense now," Zelenskyy said. "At various levels they say these are technical problems."
"Here (in Ukraine) Starlink works up to a speed of 161 km/h, then shuts off," he continued. "In the EU it works at 180-plus and works constantly. Here it shuts off in the second minute after 161 km/h and stops working. We lose both drones and connectivity."
Denys Sienik, the chargé d'affaires of Ukraine to the U.S., told CBS News in a statement later Saturday that Ukraine had still not received a response from the Pentagon or SpaceX regarding its inquiries about Starlink or Starshield service, "including confirmation that unlimited speeds have been restored and that Starshield is operating as it did previously."
Sienik said "based on the data currently available to us, we cannot confirm that these capabilities have been fully restored."
Mr. Trump told reporters on Friday he had not limited Ukraine's access to Starlink, adding he didn't believe Musk, SpaceX's CEO, was responsible either.
"Well, I don't know if it was anybody because it wasn't me, and I don't think it was Elon," Mr. Trump said while leaving the White House to travel for a rally in Georgia. "And from what I understand, it's the same as it's always been."
Musk said Wednesday he isn't responsible for deciding how Starshield is used, writing on X: "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Starshield is essential to Ukraine's armed forces as it allows personnel to communicate and carry out strikes, including by maintaining contact with drones across long distances.
On Saturday, Zelenskyy said Russia carried out a large attack on Ukraine's energy sector, targeting more than 15 critical power generation and transmission facilities across the country. A day earlier, the president said the current restrictions on Starshield had left people vulnerable to Russian drones, which was "very painful and frustrating"
Ukrainian officials and soldiers told CBS News the country's military began experiencing sudden difficulties with Starshield equipment late Tuesday, including speed limits that made it more difficult to carry out missions with fast-moving drones. Sources in Ukraine's Ministry of Defense said SpaceX had unilaterally imposed the Starshield restrictions.
Mr. Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Zelenskyy in recent days, blaming the war between Russia and Ukraine for high global energy prices. The Trump administration waived restrictions on buying Russian diesel last week in an effort to ease pressure, a move Zelenskyy argued could embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.
In a social media post on Saturday, Zelenskyy called the move "unfortunate," adding the act, championed by late Sen. Lindsey Graham, "could have helped enormously." Later, he told journalists he believed the Trump administration will lift more sanctions on Russia.
"Unfortunately, the lifting of sanctions will continue. I believe the 'diesel deal' is just the first step," Zelenskyy told reporters.
"President Trump has been clear that he wants to see this brutal war come to an end. As talks continue, this Act provides the President with additional authorities to pursue a peaceful resolution," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers told CBS News on Saturday in response to a question about lifting the sanctions. "Enforcing the sanctions provisions now would impede ongoing U.S. efforts to negotiate a durable and comprehensive peace agreement between Ukraine and Russia. The President retains the ability to exercise these authorities at any time if he determines that doing so would advance national interests."
Mr. Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to stop striking each other's energy infrastructure — announcing an "energy ceasefire" over the weekend. Zelenskyy initially said Ukraine was willing to abide by such an agreement, but that Russia's strikes never ceased, and several days later he told the Financial Times his country would no longer hold off on striking Russian refineries because Russia was still attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
The Russian government never confirmed it had agreed to a ceasefire.
In a Newsmax interview late Thursday, Mr. Trump called Zelenskyy "not a good guy for us to deal with," argued Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries would be a "disgrace," urged both sides to make a deal and said the Ukrainian leader is harder to deal with than Putin.
"I'm not a big fan of Zelenskyy," Mr. Trump said.
On Wednesday, Musk had tweeted : "Time for Zelensky to go."
Olivia  Gazis contributed to this report.
